description.narrative:
Youth Empowerment To Act (YETA) is a Refugee led Community Based Organization established in 2018 as a liquid soap making group trained by OXFAM by then called NYARENGUN (LOVE GOD) Imvepi settlement, Odupi sub-county, Terego District-Uganda. YETA is legally registered with Odupi Sub-county and Terego District.
The formation of YETA was precipitated by increased socio-economic problems associated with youth unemployment (low levels of education), limited access to education by children with disability,lack of tertiary education and vocational skills trainings which has left the youth frustrated and has resulted to drug abuse (chronic alcoholism) that triggers violence (GBV,SGBV) and other conflict related acts in the community, suicide and village crimes such as theft and vandalism of community facilities like security solar light as ways of getting money, increased economic bondage of women, poor sexual behavior that has increased the spread of HIV/AIDS amongst young people, rampart destruction of the environment, unequal involvement andparticipation of women and the minority communities in leadership and service delivery, low levels of community participation in hygiene and sanitation promotion to access clean and safe drinking water as well as cases of violence and conflicts amongst communities (Refugees and host).
Vision; To have a society with constructive, peaceful and productive self-reliant youth for inclusive service delivery and sustainability.
Mission; Commit to advocate and promote positive human values for a progressive society.
Achievements Community led mobilization; utilization the community structures such as refugee/host leaders to take lead in mobilizing and empowering communities to actively participate in community developmental and trans-formative activities. This has increased the level of women and girls’ participation in leadership and decision making in their various communities.
Community led facilitation; Meaningful involvement of local community leaders andwomen as facilitators/trainers while implementing our activities has built more confidence in both refugee and host community women and men to always take lead and inspire others. By so doing refugee and host community members feel valued and has increased and improved their participation in most activities for ownership and sustainability. We identify knowledgeable and resourceful community facilitators with rich background on peace building or activities of relevance. Theiralready existing influence asleaders greatly impacted the beneficiaries in terms of using local languages, examples above all beingfrom the same society.
Use of the GALS methodologies; Use of the GALS methodology/tools such as challenge action tree and Gender Balance Tree whichinvestigates the roots and fruits of violence and deals at depth with specific issues identified by the community members, such as anger, prejudice, stereotyping, ethnicity, etc. This approach aims at gender transformative leadership, it tries to break thebarrier that hinders women and girls’ participation and involvement in leadership and decision making at all level.
This has empowered most women to take leadership roles, participate in planning at all level, make key decisions on key family or community concerns above all it has empowered them to know their rights and to participate towards development
Partner Contribution YETA will build peace and improve social cohesion among refugees and with host communities and skills to support developmentand peace through training of women and girls on gender trans-formative leadership, human rights and peace building, Co-creating, coaching and mentor-ship programs for girls and women, Identifying and train male champions to advance women participationagenda, Mapping/ capacity assessment of Local leaders (RWCs and LCs), Facilitating, structures with tools to enhance their work, Establishing and training the alliance of cultural and religious leaders of refugees and host communities, Facilitating quarterly meetings of the alliance, Creating awareness on peace building, mental health and psychosocial support, Gender Based Violence and climate change through IEC materials, MDD, Debates, Sports, radio talk shows, spot messages and community dialogues,Mapping and undertake restoration of degraded environment, Identification, recognition and award of climate change champions among others.

1. HISTORY Youth Empowerment To Act (YETA) is a Refugee led Community Based Organization established in 2018 as a liquid soap making group trained by OXFAM by then called NYARENGUN (LOVE GOD) Imvepi settlement, Odupi sub-county, Terego District-Uganda. YETA is legally registered with Odupi Sub-county and Terego District.
The formation of YETA was precipitated by increased socio-economic problems associated with youth unemployment (low levels of education), limited access to education by children withdisability, lack of tertiary education and vocational skills trainings which has left the youth frustrated and has resulted to drug abuse (chronic alcoholism) that triggers violence (GBV,SGBV) and other conflict related acts in the community, suicide andvillage crimes such as theft and vandalism of community facilities like security solar light as ways of getting money, increased economic bondage of women, poor sexual behavior that has increased the spread of HIV/AIDS amongst young people, rampart destruction of the environment, un-equal involvement and participation of women and the minority communities in leadership and service delivery, low levels of community participation in hygiene and sanitation promotion to access clean and safe drinking water aswell as cases of violence and conflicts amongst communities (Refugees and host).
2. ACHIEVEMENTS What have been the principal results in the past three years that contribute to significant, structural, sustained and positive improvement in the lives of men, women, girls and boys suffering from poverty, injustice, insecurity and exclusion? In our past experience of other projects implemented we noted that; Peacebuilding is a vital tool to community transformation and it is a process that needs timeandresources (Long term intervention) as it involves a lot of behaviour change processes and procedures.
Community led mobilization; utilization the community structures such as refugee/host leaders to take lead in mobilizing and empowering communities toactively participate in community developmental and transformative activities. This has increased the level of women and girls’ participation in leadership and decision making in their various communities.
Community led facilitation; Meaningful involvement of local community leaders and women as facilitators/trainers while implementing our activities has built more confidence in both refugee and host community women and men to always take lead and inspire others. By so doing refugee and host communitymembers feel valued and has increased and improved their participation in most activities for ownership and sustainability. We identify knowledgeable and resourceful community facilitators with rich background on peace building or activities of relevance. Their already existing influence as leaders greatly impacted the beneficiaries in terms of using local languages, examples above all being from the same society.
Use of the GALS methodologies; Use of the GALS methodology/tools such as challenge action tree and Gender Balance Tree which investigates the roots and fruits of violence and deals at depth with specific issues identified by the community members, such as anger, prejudice, stereotyping, ethnicity, etc. This approach aims at gender transformative leadership, it tries to break the barrier that hinders women and girls’ participation and involvement in leadership and decision making at all level.
This has empowered most women to take leadership roles, participate in
planning atalllevel, make key decisions on key family or community concerns above all it has empowered them to know their rights and to participate towards development
3. INSTITUTIONAL PURPOSE Vision: To have a society with constructive, peaceful and productive self-reliant youth for inclusive service delivery and sustainability.
Mission: We commit to advocate and promote positive human values for a progressive society.
Core values  Respect of humanity and dignity.  Determination, hard work and commitment.  Responsibility, Transparency and Accountability.  Live role model lifestyle.  Gender equality.
Principle objectives Strategic area 1: - Improving access to education and skills development for the children with disability (CWD), school dropouts in Imvepi refugee settlement.
Strategic area 2: -Empowering and building sustainable self-reliant peaceful coexisting and united communities in Imvepi.
Strategic area 3: -Strengtheningcommunity mobilization, participation and capacity towardsownership and integrated sustainable WASH and Environment
Strategic area4: -Strengthening the institutional frame work, governance and resource base for YETA and attainment of a vibrant public brand presence.
Field(s) of activity: What are the principal thematic and geographic areas in which the organisation works? Who are the social actors that benefit from the work? Thematic areas of our work: Describe what you do in each (as relevant) Water Sanitation and Hygiene o Conducting community awareness and sensitization meeting o Building community based water engineering structure to work withWASH implementing partners for capacity building in possible repair, fixing and maintenance of taps and pipe leakages. o Conductinggeneral publichealthpromotions in the community which includes general cleanness and fencing of water points. o Distribution of hygiene kits (tooth paste and brush, soap, nail cutter, bucket and a pair of scissor) for children with disability.
Livelihoods o Advocacy for skills training for out of school young people and adults. o Supporting entreprenuirers with business idea, trainings start-up capital. o Talent enhancement programs and support.
Protection, Peace building, Social Cohesion • Conducting inter-groupdialogues and interactions • Organizing joint mediation • Creating conflict early warning systems (e.g. strengthening the reporting systems) • Advocacy for the existing social divisions • Mapping the peaceful coexistence dividers and connectors amongst thecommittees • Conducting community mobilization and sanitization • Building the capacity of both the refugees and the host community leaders (Youth,Women Men and the land lords) through trainings on conflict management, tolerance and conflict sensitivity. • Organizing talent enhancement programs. • Peace messaging and media (use of simple targeted messages that are age, gender and culture sensitive and carefully translated in appropriate languages to reach a wide audience. • Disseminating informationon education and communication (IEC) materials to inform individuals of the risks of community violence. • Organizing workshops and seminars for the youth, Women groups and elders to share their views on peace process in South Sudan and facilitate learning platforms and information sharing on peace process in South Sudan. • Conducting trainings and awareness campaigns about durable solutions. • Providing information to Refugees about place origin (security, legal and material safety) • Assessing POCsinterests and key motivations for return, resettled elsewherethrough FGDs, HH visits individualized interviews.
Environment and Energy o Tree planting/growing o Community mobilization and sensitization on the dangers of environmental degradation and importance/benefits of environmental protection/conservation. Education •Training parents and teachers on how to support learning of CWD (specialized support) • Conducting home based and school learning for the CWDs • Conducting community disability awareness campaigns on radio talk shows and at community • Providing technical assistance and advice for the parents and the teachers • Conducting community mobilization and sensitization on education activities to parents and school aged children •Training youths on vocational skills and life skills for self-reliance • Being highly consultative with all the stake holders focusing on technical cooperation, capacity building and implementation. • Conducting Go back to school campaigns.
Areasof operation: I. Education and Livelihood II. Peace building and MHSSP III. Integrated WASH and environment IV. Institutional development and governance
4. STRATEGIC POSITIONING Analyse the environment in which the organisationworks? Who are the other relevant social actors, including government and business, and what roles do they play? In this context, what is unique about the position of the organisation?
YETA’s COORDINATION FRAME WORK
External; UNHCR monthly sector working group meetings, settlement interagency meetings, integrated village meetings, global events planning meetings and celebrations
Internal; the success of this frame work heavily depends on diligent team work, effective communication and solid structures within YETA. At the heart of this is an effective internal coordination between program and within the entire organization on the one hand, and stakeholders on the other hand. Coordination shall be within and amongst the variousplayers who have both a direct and indirect influence over the organization, both at the lower level and higher level. Annual planning and review meetings, management meetings, team meetings quarterly meetings, monthly planning meetings, weeklyplanning meetings will be platforms for internal coordination.
